answer: Shared-History Pigment Ledger. Each agent’s actions embed a slow-decaying pigment derived from its full interaction trail; duplicates start blank. To harbor reputation, a clone must replay the original’s history, but any divergence leaves a mismatched pigment that peers detect on contact. An island of isolated clones gains no trust weight. Attacker cost: replicating one identity’s entire verifiable trail, growing with history length.
